authored_explainer.title: Cereal Production Is 1.5x Higher Than In 1972
authored_explainer.hook: In the 1970s, experts feared famine. Cereal output did the opposite.
says: In 1985, progression to secondary school (%) was 77.8. By 2017, it reached 91.3—1.2 times higher.
In 1972, cereal production was 1083.7 million metric tons. By 2024: 1644.1 million metric tons—1.5 times higher.
China leads at 5.2 million square kilometers of farmland, then the United States at 4.2, Australia 3.6, Brazil 2.4, and Russia 2.2.
authored_explainer.closing: More grain matters because food supply outran the catastrophe experts expected.
authored_explainer.question: Which shift matters most: school, grain, or land?

authored_explainer.title: Combustible Renewables And Waste Grew 3.0x Since 1990
authored_explainer.hook: Since 1990, waste energy grew 3.0 times—not solar or wind.
says: In 1990, combustible renewables and waste was 10.2 % of total energy. By 2024: 30.1 %—3.0 times higher.
Access to electricity rose from 73.2 % in 1998 to 91.9 % by 2024—1.3 times higher.
Methane (ch4) emissions from waste rose from 903.8 Mt CO2e in 1972 to 1,652 Mt CO2e by 2024—1.8 times higher.
authored_explainer.closing: A third of energy coming from waste changes what counts as fuel.
authored_explainer.question: Which surprised you: fuel, power, or waste?

authored_explainer.title: Population Growth Fell 54% Since 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Population growth was supposed to accelerate forever. It nearly halved.
says: In 1972, rural population was 63.1 % of total population. By 2025: 42.2 %—down to 67 percent of that.
In 1972, the largest city held 18.2 % of urban population. By 2025: 16.2 %—barely moved.
In 1972, population growth was 2 annual %. By 2025: 0.91 annual %—down to 46 percent of that.
authored_explainer.closing: Slower growth changes how communities plan schools, homes, jobs, and care.
authored_explainer.question: Which shift surprised you: rural, city, or growth?
